#!/usr/bin/env bash
# andesim: repo-root entry for the C++ driver (build/andesim).
# Self-bootstraps on first use so a fresh clone can run ./andesim
# directly; the build is host-only (no Verilator/SystemC/QEMU needed).
#
# macOS is run-only: both legs must share one Linux kernel, so the wrapper
# re-execs inside the prebuilt runtime image (podman machine VM); the shared
# mmap then lives in the VM, never on a virtiofs mount. ANDESIM_OS is a
# test hook to force the branch from Linux.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

if [ "${ANDESIM_OS:-$(uname -s)}" = "Darwin" ]; then
  exec bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_in_container.sh" "$@"
fi

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >&2
exec "$BIN" "$@"
=====BUILD_DRIVER.SH=====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the andesim driver: driver/ -> build/andesim.
#
# Standalone C++20 target (no Verilator, SystemC, or QEMU). Depends only on
# the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header under include/. This is the
# bootstrap consumed by setup.sh and `andesim build --what driver` (wired in
# F14). Out-of-tree build under build/driver; the binary is redirected to
# build/andesim via CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
BUILD="$ROOT/build/driver"

cmake -S "$ROOT/driver" -B "$BUILD" \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="$ROOT/build" \
  >/dev/null

cmake --build "$BUILD" -j"$(nproc)"

echo "built: $ROOT/build/andesim"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F0 contract: scaffold + build + parity harness for andesim.
#
#   1. scripts/build_driver.sh builds build/andesim (executable).
#   2. andesim with no args prints usage and exits non-zero.
#   3. andesim -h prints usage and exits zero.
#   4. tests/andes_sim/parity.sh runs (exit 0 with no cases yet).
#
# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development
# (mirrors tests/hsim/test_hsim_*.sh). Not wired into run_e2e.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

# 1. build produces an executable
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# 2. no args -> usage on output, non-zero exit
out=$("$BIN" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "no-args exit code should be non-zero, got 0"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "usage" || fail "no-args output missing 'usage':"$'\n'"$out"

[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "-h exit code should be 0, got $rc"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "usage" || fail "-h output missing 'usage':"$'\n'"$out"

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env, then the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v; v=$(cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$_LIB_ROOT/verilator/build"
}

This is the minimal step of the two-part driver scaffold: the ./andesim wrapper self-builds the standalone C++20 driver (build/andesim) on first use, so a fresh clone can run it with no Verilator, SystemC, or QEMU present. The dispatcher parses the CLI and renders the full run/list/doctor help tree, but every subcommand stubs out to a "not yet implemented" path until its handler lands feature by feature. The subcommand table carries NO archive/replay slots -- that half-built snapshot/replay workflow is never added in this series. The completion step adds the argv/json/strutil/config_env helpers plus the unit-test infra (cli_test, json_test, infra_test) that exercises this same parser. test_andes_sim_f0.sh is authored golden-free: it asserts the build produces an executable, no-arg prints usage and exits non-zero, and -h prints usage and exits zero, dropping the retired parity.sh step.
